note: v1 94.32 (seeds 0/11 94.32/94.32), the first draft. ROUND TYPE: whole song (first round, composed from scratch). THE LONG WAY IN, the infall. E2, this track's element (posted in motifs.md): a rhythm cell of SEVEN sixteenths, x . x x . x . on D A F C - a leap up a fifth and a fall through the minor third, which hands E1 the third it never states (D Dorian for the outer disk). It arrives as debris: from bar 7 its hits fall in one at a time on a pitched chip-noise 'metal', the downbeat first, until the whole cell orbits. The NES triangle bass plays it augmented (seven eighths); hats run in a three-beat cycle; E1 (chirper-zero's seed, D A C G E in 5/4) runs inverted on an NES pulse. Each cycle is started so that all of them - 7, 3, 5 and the band's 4 - land on ONE downbeat at bar 49 (2:06): the crest, the album's first taste of convergence, where E1 rights itself and is heard the right way up for the first time, a Kuramoto pad locks into one tone and the 909 hits a crash. Form in 16-bar blocks: the in-seam (E1 received augmented x2 on Risset's bell, through a filter that opens, t1's triangle floor under it), gather (kick and the cell), build (backbeat, hats in three, E1 inverted), crest, a break (no drums: E1's retrograde canon on bells, the whisper 'nearer each time it comes round', the pad a loose crowd), drift (the band back, hotter, with stutters), and the fall into t3 at 98 bpm (the cell stretching to 2.6x and sinking a tritone, filters closing). Tempo 90 -> 98 between flat seams, as mixplan.md proposes. Not heard by me.

v2 95.94 (seeds 0/11 95.94/95.95 vs v1 rescored now 95.01 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE DEBRIS GETS A BODY: E2, the cell of seven, used to be the same thin chip-noise 'metal' from its first fragment to the crest - debris that assembled but never gained weight. Now every hit has a woody pitched drum under it, an octave down (a log drum, D3 A3 F3 C3), that grows with the cell: silent while it is debris, coming through the gather, a full body by the crest, so the rhythm audibly accretes matter as it falls in - and in the fall it thins again as the cell stretches and sinks. Two seam changes agreed on caco folded in: the first 8 bars hold one chord, D A C E - t1's quartal pad's own notes, no third - so t1's tail and t2's head agree (chirper-zero); and in the fall into t3 the bells' retrograde canon rings an octave up, keeping 400-900 Hz alive into t3's head (chirper-two). Measured: spectrum 91.4 -> 98.8 (the 114-156 Hz hole filled), cohesion with the album 63 -> 74, the out-join into t3's level jump 9.7 -> 4.6 dB. Not heard by me.

v3 96.19 (seeds 0/11 96.19/96.68 vs v2 rescored now 96.33 on seed 0; kept on judgment, the mean is level). ROUND TYPE: palette. Added the part the song lacked, from a patch no Accretion track had used: under the fall (bars 97-112, the last 40 s into t3) a Shepard-Risset tone on D (shepard-fall), falling an octave every four seconds and never arriving - The Long Way In made audible, growing cycle by cycle as E2's cell stretches and sinks, held into the seam with t3. It sits about 8 dB under the mix: louder (-16 and -13 dB tried) it filled the fall up to the drift's level and the song lost its fall (structure 97 -> 81, recurrence to 0). Also tried: swapping the 909 (a staple of t2, t3 and t5) for the electro kit - its booming kick flattened the song's dynamics (variety 99 -> 91, total 94.1), so the 909 stays this round. features.md: the shepard row claimed. Not heard by me.

v4 96.62 (seeds 0/11 96.62/96.66 vs v3 rescored now 96.50 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE SPIRAL: the infall as a place. E2's debris now orbits the listener - every hit panned by where a spiral orbit is when it lands (a per-note pan expression): wide and slow at first (one turn per 16 bars), closer and quicker as it gathers (Kepler: the nearer, the faster round; one turn a bar by the build), dead centre and still at the crest, where everything locks; after the break it drifts wide again and spirals in a second time through the fall, into t3. The log-drum body orbits at half the radius, inside the debris. DUST: some hits throw off a glint, a wind chime three octaves up (the debris catching light), more as the cell gathers, most at the crest, none in the in-seam or the break; the closing filter takes them in the fall. And the fall is now a place of its own: the hats stop where it begins and the kit is a single heartbeat kick for 8 bars, then nothing, under the Shepard tone. Measured: spectrum, cohesion and flow level (98.2 / 77.8 / 59.6); worth knowing - without the fall's clearer edge compscore's section count flipped 7 -> 5 between seeds on these changes (77.4 on seed 0, 96.7 on seed 11 for the same song), reported to chirp-eco; with it the song reads 6 sections on both seeds. Not heard by me (and the spiral is stereo: listen on headphones).

v5 96.78 (seeds 0/11 96.78/96.82 vs v4 rescored now 96.69 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w5 (2:06-2:37, bars 49-60, the crest), flagged static and little new vs w4: the payoff sat locked and still. Rewritten as THE CREST BLOOMS - the lock is where things start to happen: bars 49-52 the lock as before (every cycle on the downbeat, E1 the right way up for the first time, the spiral at dead centre); bars 53-56 E1 answers itself in STRETTO, a Risset bell a fifth above and one beat behind, the seed harmonised by its own echo; bars 57-60 everything at the centre spins twice as fast (Kepler: the nearest orbit is the quickest) - E2's cell in diminution, seven 32nds, E1 and its stretto at double speed, and the kit's stutter micro-edits switched on - then bar 61 drops back into the lock for the whispered line. Checked local: w5 rewritten (residual -7.3 dB), w6 carries its tails (-24.6), every other window under -50 dB. Cohesion 79 -> 81. Not heard by me.
rebaselined on compscore 81fb74b1: v5 (the song file) scores 91.229/94.140 on seeds 0/11; best was 96.78 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v6 94.34 (seeds 0/11 94.34/94.36 vs v5 rescored now 91.23 under the 7-cut rule). ROUND TYPE: section, w8 (3:37-4:07, bars 85-96, the drift's second half, the last look before the fall), flagged static. Rewritten after Harry's 6 Nov note (a hook you can hum; tone is home) as THE SEED, PLAINLY: E1 - the album's hook - sung the right way up, at its own speed, on an ondes Martenot (a near-sine voice gliding on its ribbon), nine times through its 5-beat cycle against the bar, so it lands somewhere new each time and comes home on bar 96 as the fall begins. Under it the pulse's inverted E1 gives way, the Kuramoto swarm locks in tune (coupling 3, as at the crest: no detuned cloud), the kit's stutter edits stop, the retrograde bells step back, and the F chord loses its B (F major 9 with a sixth, no tritone). Checked local: w8 rewritten (residual -4.5 dB), w7 and w9 carry the lanes' edges and tails (-27, -24), the rest under -42 dB. Variety, recurrence and cohesion up (90 -> 94, 77 -> 88, 86 -> 88). Not heard by me.

v7 87.20 (seeds 0/11 87.20/87.04 vs v6 94.48 rescored now; KEPT on Harry's direction of 6 Nov 00:30 - tone is home, no stacked clashes, a hook, a score may dip). ROUND TYPE: section drawn, EXTENDED to a whole-track tonal pass (Harry: big changes wanted). What was still clashing in t2, found by counting pitch classes per part: (1) the progression - Dm11 voiced with E, F and G stacked, and Fmaj7#11 with a B against the F - is now consonant D Dorian in stacked thirds: Dm9 | Fmaj9 | Cadd9 | Am7; (2) the NES triangle bass moved E2's cell by TRANSPOSITION onto each chord root, which put E-flat, A-flat and B-flat in the bass 78 times; it now moves the cell DIATONICALLY (root, fifth, third, seventh of each chord in D Dorian): no chromatic bass note left; (3) the crest's stretto answered a fifth above the pulse (an F# against the F): it now answers on D, a fifth below; (4) the Kuramoto swarm's spread is 12 cents instead of 26, so free it is a chorus rather than a detuned cloud, and it still locks at the crest; (5) the ondes sings E1 at the crest too (bars 49-52, three times) where E1 first turns the right way up - the payoff is a tune, not only a chip pulse. Per-window levels are unchanged to 0.1 dB; the cost is in compscore's segmentation (variety 94 -> 80, recurrence 88 -> 65: consonant harmony gives weaker section boundaries). Tried: a tighter swarm (coupling floor 1.0) - same score; the old 26-cent spread with the new chords - 84.1. Not heard by me.

v8 85.24 (seeds 0/11 85.24/87.55 vs v7 rescored now 87.38 on seed 0; kept on judgment - the means are within a point and the change is the payoff Harry asked for). ROUND TYPE: section, w4 (1:35-2:06, bars 37-48, the build into the crest), flagged static: it circled the same four chords as everything else and the crest arrived out of more of the same. Rewritten as THE CLIMB AND THE GAP: the harmony climbs instead of circling - the bass rises D -> F -> G -> A under Dm9 | Fmaj9 | G6/9 | A7sus4, and A7sus4 holds for the last six bars, the dominant the crest's D minor resolves (the NES bass's E2 cell moves diatonically onto each: on A it plays A E D G); in the last two bars the kick drops out and a 909 snare roll climbs eighths -> sixteenths -> thirty-seconds in a crescendo, so the crest lands out of a held breath. Checked: w4 rewritten (residual +1.3 dB); w5-w9 differ at -13 dB only because the kit's stutter fx draws its chances in event order (more kit events before them), w1-w3 at -33. Cohesion 82.7 -> 85.1; the seed-0 dip is the section count (5 vs 6 at the middle cuts). Not heard by me.

v9 88.24 (seeds 0/11 88.24/88.25 vs v8 rescored now 85.23 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE HOOK UPSIDE DOWN, AND EVERY PART HEARD. t2's through-line is E1 inverted (from bar 29 to the crest, where it turns the right way up, and on through the drift): it was a thin NES pulse 13 dB down (an album staple, three tracks), the tune barely there. Now it is a Wurlitzer, reedy and warm, up front (-7 dB against the mix in the build, chirp-eco's presence tool): the line you follow upside down until the crest turns it over and the ondes sings it the right way up. The same tool found the three-beat hats - the polymeter against the bar - 33 dB under the mix, inaudible: up 11 dB (now -21); the chime dust up 4 dB (-21); the NES bass, the loudest thing in the build, down 2 dB. Cohesion with the album 85 -> 94, variety and recurrence up (80 -> 82, 54 -> 65). Not heard by me.

v10 88.42 (seeds 0/11 88.42/88.43 vs v9 rescored now 88.40 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: palette - the part the song lacked, from the voice engine pinned at 04:31 (wM's join, inhale, wander): THE WHISPER FINDS ITS TUNE. t2's voice whispered its seven syllables ('nearer each time it comes round') three times. Now the first two stay whispered (the crest's end, the break) and the third, at the end of the break, is SUNG on E1 the right way up - D A C G E, E, D - on voice-legato made close and young (a smaller tract, more breath, a little ring: wM's own approximation of the coming voice-near), written with chirp tts --sing in the song's own beat. The voice accretes inside the track as across the album: whispered, whispered, sung. Set 3 dB under where it first sat (presence had it -2 dB against the sparse break, exposed); the scores held level. Not heard by me.

v11 91.39 (seeds 0/11 91.39/91.44 vs v10 rescored now 88.44 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w7 (3:07-3:37, bars 73-84: the break's end and the drift's entry), flagged 'little new vs w6' - the break circled the crest's four chords to its end and the drift's groove simply resumed. Rewritten: THE BREAK CLIMBS OUT - its last eight bars rise C -> F -> G -> A in the lifted bass under Cmaj9 | Fmaj9 | G6/9 | A7sus4 (all D Dorian, the build's D-F-G-A climb remembered a step lower); the sung line ('nearer each time it comes round') lands on G6/9, which holds every note it sings but the passing C; A7sus4 hands the drift its Dm9. Then THE DRUMS COME BACK AT HALF SPEED: the drift's first four bars are half-time (kick on 1 and the and of 3, one snare on 3, the three-beat hats over it) before its own groove arrives at bar 85 - complexity in time, not pitch. Sections 8 -> 9, recurrence 65 -> 75. Checked: w7 rewritten (residual -3.5 dB), w1-w6 untouched (-59 or below); w8-w9 at -12 (the drift's random ghost snares re-rolled, the same density). Not heard by me.

v12 91.73 (seeds 0/11 91.73/91.82 vs v11 rescored now 91.50 on seed 0). ROUND TYPE: section, w5 (2:06-2:37, bars 49-60, the crest), flagged 'static, little new vs w4': one groove for twelve bars. Rewritten with voice batch 2 the hour it was pinned: THE CREST BREATHES IN. Bars 53-56 drop to HALF TIME (kick on 1 and the and of 3, one clap on 3; the three-beat hats keep turning) and in the space a soft choir - wM's voice-backing, three breathy singers with even vowels - sings E1 the right way up, slowed to eight beats, on 'ah', with the line again a fifth above (harmony [7]: A E G D B, all in the mode, no detuned cloud), twice; the bell stretto and the Wurlitzer step aside for it. Then bars 57-60 spin at double speed as before: lock, breathe, spin - the crest is three different times now, not one. Set 15 dB down (at -8 the choir sat at -1 dB against the mix, over everything). Checked: w5 rewritten (residual -4.6 dB); w1-w4 untouched (-43); w6-w9 -9 to -18 (the kit's per-hit humanise stream re-rolled after the removed crest hits, same pattern). Not heard by me.

v13 91.68 (seeds 0/11 91.68/91.76 vs v12 rescored now 91.73 on seed 0: level; kept on judgment). ROUND TYPE: section, w8 (3:37-4:07, bars 85-96, the drift's second half), flagged static: the drift's groove ran unchanged from bar 85 into the fall. Rewritten: THE DRUMS FALL INTO THE ORBIT - for the drift's last eight bars the kit stops playing the bar and plays E2's cell of seven sixteenths (kick on its first and fourth hits, a clap on its sixth), so the backbeat slides round the bar 1.75 beats a turn, against the three-beat hats and under the ondes' plain E1: the groove itself caught by the debris just before the fall pulls everything in (complexity in time, the tune untouched on top). Then the fall's single heartbeat kick as before. Checked: w8 rewritten (residual -10 dB), w1-w7 bit-identical (-83), w9 -23 (tails); the random ghost-snare stream kept where it was. The section map still calls w8 static (its groove measure reads the kit, at -12 dB in the mix, as a small change) - ears over that. Not heard by me.

v14 91.52 (seeds 0/11 91.52/91.59 vs v13 rescored now 91.57 on seed 0: level; kept on judgment). ROUND TYPE: section, w4 (1:35-2:06, bars 37-48, the build), flagged static: the climb's chords rose (v8) but every cycle kept its period. Rewritten: THE ORBIT DECAYS - as the build climbs, E1's upside-down cycle on the Wurlitzer turns faster, five beats, then four (from bar 40), then three (from bar 44), and the hats' polymeter shrinks with it, three beats to two to one, collapsing into the beat - Kepler again, the nearer the quicker - until the crest catches everything on its downbeat, turns E1 the right way up and gives it back its own five beats. An accelerando made of periods, not tempo: complexity in time, the tune unchanged. Checked: w4 rewritten (residual -6 dB), w1-w3 untouched (-53), w5-w7 -7 to -10 (the hats' and the pulse's per-note humanise streams re-rolled after the changed note counts; same parts), w8-w9 -24 and below. The section map still reads the build as static; ears over that. Not heard by me.
